Maya Patel: Quick heads-up — followup from the RFC: we need a pragmatic ops heuristic for onboarding that keeps bench cost down but still catches regressions. Thoughts?

Jon Kim: TL;DR: agree. We should split the onboarding bench into two tiers: lightweight fast smoke + periodic deeper bench. Lightweight runs on submission, deep bench runs on scheduled canaries.

Sophie Li: +1. Also we need explicit escape hatches for models that fail only on deep bench but are otherwise OK. We should gate by severity (latency/cost/accuracy).

Leo Grant: Ops concern: dev teams will want faster feedback. If deep bench is nightly only, they might bypass it. We should add a soft canary flag that blocks promoted models only if failure rate > threshold.

Maya Patel: Proposal: (1) quick preflight ~2–5 min smoke (golden inputs + seqlen samples) that must pass; (2) async deep bench (costly) that gives a degradation score and a warning window; (3) canary routing that initially sends 1% traffic and auto-rolls back on SLO breaches.

Jon Kim: Implementation note — make smoke deterministic: stable tokenizer, fixed seeds, and a tiny golden set per model family. Keep smoke runner in the intake service so it’s cheap.

Sophie Li: We also need compatibility checks: tokenization parity, kv-cache shape, dtype/quantization support. Suggested quick probes: export minimal signature checks and run a tiny inference for KV warmup.

Leo Grant: Ops-bot suggests adding telemetry points: smoke_pass, smoke_latency_p95, deepbench_score, kv_shape_mismatch, tokenizer_diff_ratio. Those metrics should be on the model object in the registry.

ops-bot: automation note — adding metric hooks to intake pipeline: smoke_pass (bool), bench_score (float), canary_status (string). See /ops/ingest-metrics.yaml for naming.

Maya Patel: Tradeoffs to call out in RFC followup: more smoke inputs => fewer false negatives but higher cost. Smaller golden set => faster but higher risk of misses. We need an evidence-driven knob.

Jon Kim: For bench slimdown: sample by workload SKU (chat vs. completions vs. embeddings). Some families can share golden inputs. We can compress sequences by token bucketing to reduce compute.

Sophie Li: On interface boundaries: intake should return a concise acceptance payload: {artifact_id, smoke_pass, bench_score, kv_signature, tokenizer_fingerprint}. Keep it minimal so downstream services (registry, deployer) can act without re-running.

Leo Grant: Operational escape hatches: manual override with audit trail; timed quarantines (auto-unquarantine after X days unless updated); and a fast rollback play if canary errors spike.

Maya Patel: Concern: teams will game thresholds. We need periodic audits and a guardrail that escalates to security/reliability for high-cost/PII models.

Jon Kim: On quantized models: add a "shadow quant" path where we run quantized inference in parallel for a small subset to compare outputs before allowing quantized-only routing. That reduces surprises.

Sophie Li: Add a small fuzzy-match metric for semantic drift — token-level diffs are noisy for some LMs. Use an embedding-based similarity on golden outputs for deeper bench.

Leo Grant: Timeline suggestion: prototype smoke runner + telemetry in 2 sprints, wire minimal acceptance payload, then iterate on deep bench config.

Maya Patel: Action items: Jon to sketch intake API payload today; Sophie to propose golden set heuristics; Leo to list telemetry names and alert thresholds. I'll collect and add to the RFC followup doc.

Jon Kim: I'll mock the intake JSON and example responses and post later. Quick note: keep the JSON stable so downstream schema evolves slowly.

Sophie Li: Also adding a short runbook for operators: what to do when smoke fails vs deep bench warns. Short checklists are key.

Leo Grant: Agree. Ops runbook should include: quick revert command, canary throttling knobs, how to tag a model as "quarantine:manual" in the registry.

Maya Patel: Thanks all — this is a good direction. I'll open the RFC followup with these specifics and attach a minimal data spec. We'll iterate on the golden inputs strategy after the first prototype.
